description: base and head are two commits on branches that diverge from a common root commit; the root does not contain either branch's addition. A naive base-to-head diff would report base_only as removed and head_only as added, wrongly implying a regression. Comparing against the true merge-base (root) shows only head_only as new and does not implicate base_only at all, since it never existed on head's line of history.

unchanged_symbols.note: base_fn exists identically on every branch and must not appear in either diff interpretation.

direct_diff_note: Comparing base (base-branch tip) directly against head (head-branch tip) makes base_only look removed (present_in base, absent_in head) and head_only look added (absent_in base, present_in head) -- as if one feature replaced the other.
merge_base_diff_note: Comparing the merge-base (root-branch tip) against head shows only head_only as added; base_only is absent from root too, so it is not part of this change at all -- it is unrelated work still in flight on the other branch.
